_comment: LIB-ABI adjudication ledger (docs/endgame-plan.md D-E3): every OUTWARD callee of the migrated modules that has no C++ body carries a class here. The 689 already-translated callees are NOT rows -- their disposition (rebind) is derived by gen_libmh_calls.py from the migration ledgers. Populated 2026-09-01 by an 8-batch read-only fan-out + central reconciliation (tools/oneoff/2026-09-01-build-libmh-ledger.py); hand-maintained from here on. gen_libmh_calls.py --check refuses an unadjudicated callee. Classes: translate | host-callback:{render-notify,sound,platform,map-io} | event-channel:{event,screen,invalidate} (LIFT-EVQ/NOTIFY/SCREEN: lifted off the fine table onto the designed notify surface, libmh_host_events.h) | deleted (SIMABI-HOOKS 2026-09-10: the entry left the host table and libmh makes NO call in its place -- a TERMINAL class, kept as the record of the decision; gen_libmh_calls exempts it from the orphan gate and fails if a migrated module ever calls the name again) | cfg-snapshot | crt | dead | mixed (needs splitting at LIB-ABI) | unsure (needs a decision). VENDORED CALLEES ARE NOT ROWS, for the same reason translated ones are not: the row records an adjudication for a callee with no C++ body, and once a body exists the disposition is a fact about the code rather than a decision in a table. The sprintf family (12 shapes over utils_sprintf@0x4cfb9c and w_sprintf@0x4d0320, 39 sites) left this ledger on 2026-09-08 when crt/crt_sprintf.h supplied the bodies and crt/crt_select.h routed the sites through MH_CRT(); its reasoning lives in that header's banner and its oracle is `net_selftest crttest`. A NEW site spelled mh::call::w_sprintf__* would come back as unadjudicated, which is the ratchet working, not a regression. The two `host-callback:chat` rows -- llm_ui_chat_recalc_target_mode @0x0049d631 and llm_ui_chat_target_add @0x0049d5c1 -- left the same way on 2026-09-10 (SIMABI-CHAT), for the same stated reason: libmh now has BODIES for them (libmh/lockstep/lt_chat_ally_mask.cpp), so the disposition is a fact about the code and the reasoning lives in that header's banner. NOT the `deleted` class, which would be a false claim here: libmh does make a call in their place -- its own -- and the ORIGINALS stay live for the untranslated UI callers (llm_ui_chat_target_remove, llm_ui_diplomacy_apply_and_resume), which is the dual-writer story the row would have had no way to say.

GetResourseFilePtr.reason: Copy a named record from the game's packed resource files (gfx, glyphs, mission bytes, AI scripts, base layouts) into the CALLER's buffer: at most `dst_cap` bytes, returning the asset's FULL length so a caller can detect truncation, or -1 if there is no such asset. `dst` may be null when `dst_cap` is 0 -- the size query, which loads nothing. A COPY, not a pointer, and that is the point: the entry used to hand back the host's own allocation and two sim sites FREED it through the vendored CRT (a cross-heap free that breaks any host not allocating from the game's heap). mh.dll's binder does ptr -> copy -> the game's own free internally, so retail behaviour is unchanged and no libmh site owns a host pointer.

tact_frozen.reason: Return a pointer to a named record inside the game's packed resource files (gfx, glyphs, mission bytes): a generic loader, not map-specific. tact/ reads the returned bytes and, at one site, the two 16-bit header words in front of them; it never frees the pointer, so the allocation must stay valid for the rest of the session. THE FROZEN SHAPE: the sim side reshaped this entry to asset_read (a copy) at SIMABI-VFS; tact's copy keeps the pointer-returning form, which is exactly what duplication is for.

cfg_ReadMapFile.reason: PRE-FORK ONLY (DEFER-BLOB). Parse a .MP map file into the caller's map_header. AND IT IS NOT PURE IO, which is the thing to carry across: it writes real sim geometry -- width/height, and through llm_map_setup_dimensions the torus masks and pathfinder_params->width_mask. A host that returns only the header fields it thinks matter breaks pathfinding. The group is called map-io because that is how these entries reach the disk; six of the seven are PARSES wearing an io hat. Kept as-is pre-fork by the 2026-09-03 decision, superseded fork-side by the LIB-WORLD blob. NOTE the buffer contract: it writes PAST mh_cfg_struct_map_header's 0x17c for maps carrying the mission tail (measured high-water 0x189), which is why libmh hands it 0x248 bytes of backing. WHAT LIB-WORLD'S BLOB MUST CARRY TO RETIRE THIS ENTRY -- the parse OUTPUT libmh consumes, not the .MP bytes (re-verified at SIMABI-MAPIO 2026-09-10 against the body @0x004a3b9d and both libmh sites): (1) the globals `width` and `height` (RID_WIDTH / RID_HEIGHT, 4 B each, MF_VIEW|MF_MEASURED|MF_SAVE); (2) `current_map_data.tlo_name` (+0x11c, 12 B, RID_CURRENT_MAP_DATA) -- the tileset NAME, which is what the parse produces. THE RESOLVED TLO INDEX IS NOT THIS ENTRY'S OUTPUT, corrected here: it is one hop downstream, libmh's own body calling cfg_GetTloIndex on that string (sim/libtrans/sim_lt_cfg_planet.cpp:113), and since LIFT-TABLE S3 the index crosses host-side inside LIBMH_EVK_INV_PLANET_GFX_SETUP rather than landing in a region at all. Both libmh sites read the header back for tlo_name and nothing else (sim_lt_cfg_planet.cpp:113; sim/resid/sim_start_tutorial.cpp:148, which strcpy's it into the HASHED Planets[0x1f].tlo_file), and both DISCARD the return -- the `< 0` failure test exists only in the untranslated lobby callers (llm_lobby_map_transfer_finalize, llm_cfg_map_verify_version). THE TORUS MASKS ARE NOT BLOB FIELDS EITHER: general.{width_mask,height_mask,big_width,big_height,bw_mask,bh_mask} and pathfinder_params->width_mask are DERIVED from width/height by llm_map_setup_dimensions @0x004989c2, a body libmh already owns translated and shadow-armed (sim/libtrans/sim_lt_map_setup_dimensions.cpp) and already re-invokes on the load path (save/save_live.cpp:466). It could not be otherwise for the pathfinder byte: its storage is a malloc'd 0x20-byte block reached through general.pathfinder_params (+0xc), heap and NOT a bound region, so a step-0 region dump cannot capture it and the importer must re-derive. Written but NOT consumed by libmh, hence not blob fields: header player_count/checksum/file_size/footer (the lobby transfer check and version verifier read those) and the global `version`. THE NAME IS DELIBERATELY THE ORIGINAL ONE (SIMABI-NAMES, 2026-09-10), and it is the pre-fork stamp: every other surviving entry was renamed to an abstract name that promises a permanent host contract, which is exactly the promise a DEFER-BLOB row does not make -- this entry is scheduled to LEAVE the surface when LIB-WORLD's blob carries the outputs listed above. An abstract name here would read as an obligation a standalone host must implement forever; the original callee's name says instead 'this is the pre-fork binary's own parse, still here because the blob is not'.

file_seek.reason: Set a handle's position: `whence` 0 = from the start, 1 = from the current position, 2 = from the end. Returns 0 on success. NOT AN ORIGINAL-GRAPH EDGE: libmh's own container writer authored these calls (libmh/save/save_live.cpp) to learn an already-written per-planet file's length, which the original does with the same primitive. SIMABI-VFS tried to retire this pair by threading the written byte count instead, and the retirement is UNSOUND -- see vfs_tell. (The routing census reports 0 direct callers for this entry and for vfs_tell; that is the census's blind spot for libmh-authored calls, not a dead entry -- both are verified live in src/mh_dll.)

file_tell.reason: Report a handle's position, and must agree with what vfs_seek accepts. Same provenance as vfs_seek. THE PAIR IS PERMANENT, not a leftover: the .sav embeds EVERY visited planet's save%02d.dat size-prefixed, and those files are written by three separate original roots (game_SaveGame 0x0044719a, SwitchToPlanet 0x0044cece, try_enter_tactical_mission 0x0044d38f), two of them untranslated and at arbitrary earlier instants -- so at most one member's length is ever knowable from the writing path. The container learns the other lengths from the files.

game_ui_PrintTextMessage.reason: LIFT-NOTIFY text surface (2026-09-03, slice 4): converted to LIBMH_EVTK_TEXT_MAIN over libmh_set_text_sink/libmh_poll_texts -- composition stays at the sites (non-hashed scratch), the emit carries the composed UTF-16 string (sync sink gets the caller's pointer, queue mode copies), the hosted sink routes onto the original thunk. Original reason: forward to AddTextToPrintQueue.

getAsciiVer.reason: Convert a wide (UTF-16) string to the local ANSI code page and return the converted bytes. STRICT CONTRACT (SIMABI-STRING 2026-09-10): reproduce the bytes Win32's WideCharToMultiByte(CP_ACP, ...) produces on the machine's own ANSI code page -- an equivalent encoding is NOT a substitute, and an ASCII truncation is exact for this build's own text and silently wrong for a non-ASCII text table. THE 'misfit -> init data' LINE IS REFUTED (measured 2026-09-09): this is that call, the structural twin of utils_wide_to_short_str, live from nine sites -- error dialogs, building construct, the lobby map picker -- not a boot-time table. AND IT FEEDS HASHED SIM STATE, which this row denied until 2026-09-10 and is the correction it now carries: llm_strat_planet_session_begin passes the returned pointer to llm_strat_player_profile_init as name_str (sim/resid/sim_planet_session_begin.cpp), whose body -- decompiled at 0x00454985, the byte-pair copy loop at the top -- copies it into _G_LLM_STRAT_PLAYERS[player].name (0x00cff060, stride 0x740), inside the 14848-byte `strat_players` slice HIDX_STRAT_PLAYERS, hashed RAW with no mask. So wide_to_local is NOT 'the one entry in this table whose result feeds hashed state': THERE ARE TWO, and a host whose codec returns different bytes here diverges on the very next state hash exactly as it would there. MEASURED, not argued: simtest's sim_planet_session_begin T12 flips one byte of this entry's returned buffer at that sim site and the `strat_players` slice hash moves, and reverting it restores the hash exactly. THE CP_ACP MULTIPLAYER HAZARD IS A NAMED DEFERRED DECISION OWNED BY LIB-FORK (first bites at LIB-REF, whose headless host must either implement the locale codec or declare the divergence): two peers on two Windows locales hash different bytes, which is retail's own behaviour, and vendoring a fixed codec into libmh would fix it while breaking R5's hosted premise -- so it is a declared, user-approved divergence taken at its own slice on the llm_strat_rng_seed_wallclock_seconds precedent, NEVER a silent vendor. RULED 2026-09-12 (F0-CPACP, user): KEEP CP_ACP -- retail-faithful, the same-locale MP requirement documented; the post-fork direction is full UTF-8/multilanguage text (docs/fork-plan.md, post-F5), which retires this question rather than re-answering it.

gfx_LoadSprite.reason: LIFT-TACT slice B (2026-09-09): converted to LIBMH_EVK_INV_TACT_CURSOR_SPRITE {a=sprite id}. An asset ID, not a bitmap. Its one libmh site is llm_tact_frame's cursor pick, and the id is chosen from LAST frame's hovered_unit_id -- render_view updates that at step 15, after -- which is the original's own ordering and is preserved by the synchronous-at-emit dispatch.

llm_build_media_diag_report.reason: Produce the 0x400-byte media/CD diagnostic block libmh appends as the last block of a .sav. WHAT A HOST SUPPLIES: 0x400 bytes. THE CONTENTS ARE INERT, measured rather than assumed: the function has exactly two call sites image-wide (the main-menu load, which discards the return, and game_SaveGame), and llm_game_load stops at its last wanted member and never reads another byte -- traced to its utils_close_file, and independently recorded in docs/save-format.md. So a fixed placeholder satisfies the format and nobody needs to issue an mciSendCommandA CD/TOC query. IT STAYS REQUIRED RATHER THAN BECOMING A LIBMH-INTERNAL PLACEHOLDER, which is where the plan's 'reclasses toward internal/stub' line ran out: libmh generating the placeholder itself would make the HOSTED save differ from the original's byte-for-byte, and this entry is exactly the seam that lets mh.dll keep producing the real bytes while a standalone host produces any 0x400 it likes.

llm_cam_jump_queue_clear.reason: LIFT-NOTIFY slice 2 (2026-09-03): converted to LIBMH_EVK_CAM_JUMP_QUEUE_CLEAR. Void, scalar payload; hosted sink routes onto the thunk synchronously at emit; mh::state::evt adapter keeps the member signature identical.

llm_debug_log_msg_stub.reason: DELETED FROM THE SURFACE at SIMABI-HOOKS (2026-09-10). The game's debug-log sink, gutted in retail (0x004ee8df, stack probe + return, re-verified in the DB) -- the message pointer is never read, so the string was never emitted in retail either. Its one libmh site was ai_reinforcements' no-candidate path. Nothing may call it again.

llm_fatal_cleanup.reason: Release the game's own resources on the fatal path, ahead of utils_abort. Also called from two TACTICAL bodies that are not parsers (tact_door, tact_unit_spawn), which is why it survives the mission-load cluster's disposition. It must be safe to call with the world inconsistent -- that is the only state it is ever called in.

llm_game_save_player_data.reason: Write the per-player profile block. Byte-compatible output is a permanent guarantee of the frozen side, so this is a format obligation rather than a convenience.

llm_gfx_apply_resolution_change.reason: REQUIRED under R3b (class flipped to match at LIFT-TABLE S1, 2026-09-09 -- the row said KEPT REQUIRED in prose while shipping notify:1, i.e. telling a headless host it could bind a no-op).  KEPT REQUIRED under R3b (LIFT-TACT slice B2, 2026-09-09), same reversal and same reason as its sibling llm_gfx_apply_window_resolution. Closure 107 functions, sixteen regions read by translated libmh. The same-call readback is measured rather than assumed: it writes MAP_REGION_LIST_HEAD, and llm_tact_mission_end_return_to_strategic calls map_LoadPlanetFromDisk on the very next line, which reaches llm_map_region_pool_reset / merge_small_regions / recompute_adjacency (checked against the committed call graph).

llm_gfx_apply_window_resolution.reason: REQUIRED under R3b (class flipped to match at LIFT-TABLE S1, 2026-09-09 -- the row said KEPT REQUIRED in prose while shipping notify:1, i.e. telling a headless host it could bind a no-op).  KEPT REQUIRED under R3b (LIFT-TACT slice B2, 2026-09-09) -- the conversion was WRITTEN and then REVERTED on the gate's measurement, which is the epistemics clause doing its job. Its closure is 81 functions and it re-derives fifteen regions translated libmh reads, including GFX_DRAW_SURFACE and FRAMEBUFFER -- and llm_tact_mission_start, the one emitter, reads BOTH later in the SAME CALL: the 480-row intro blit at tact_mission_start.cpp:150-151 uses gfx_draw_surface as its source and gfx_framebuffer as its destination. A frame-edge drain would run that blit between the old surface pointers. This is not a notification, it is the host reconfiguring the display and libmh depending on the result, which is exactly the case R3b makes required-class.

Every libmh site discarded the descriptor pointer it returned (dead stack stores at 0x004bad0f/0x004bad41), and its only remaining consumer was the tutorial hint widget's layout, which is host-side now. llm_gfx_load_planet_extra_sprite_banks.reason: CONVERTED at SIMABI-NOTIFY (2026-09-10) to LIBMH_EVK_INV_PLANET_EXTRA_SPRITE_BANKS, no payload. The row's own previous text is what licensed it: PURELY PRESENTATION since LIFT-TABLE S2/S3 (nothing it touches is hashed; the host owns the bank[] table it walks), sitting in the map-io group only because it reaches the disk the same way -- and its notify:false was that group's class string, not a measurement of this entry (the S1 trap, uncaught for this row). Section 0a's direction settles the rest: a gfx leaf leaves. Its one libmh site (save_live.cpp:462, 0x00448649) is void, unconditional, and the last statement of run_ours_load_planet before `return 1`, so nothing is consumed (R3) and nothing is read back by the emitter (R3b). Its subtree is a SUBSET of LIBMH_EVK_INV_ALL_SPRITE_BANKS's -- the original llm_gfx_load_all_sprite_banks calls it -- so the sprite-table readers carry that scope's already-measured later-frame disposition.

llm_gfx_ui_sprite_get_header_field2.reason: Absorbed into LIBMH_EVK_SCR_TUT_HINT_LAYOUT, same reasoning as llm_gfx_sprite_width above.

llm_gfx_view_metrics_init.reason: LIFT-TACT slice B2 (2026-09-09): converted to LIBMH_EVK_INV_GFX_VIEW_METRICS. This one had a REAL R3b readback at the time slice B2 was measured -- it writes _G_LLM_GFX_PANEL_ROW_SKIP, which llm_tact_ui_sel_panel_init read three times in the same mission_start call chain -- and it dissolved rather than being argued away: slice A moved that draw head host-side, and _G_LLM_GFX_PANEL_ROW_SKIP now has ZERO translated readers (all five remaining references are in mh.dll's own sink). Re-measured after slice A landed, not assumed.

llm_input_key_dequeue.reason: Pop the next key event from the host's input queue, or report empty. REQUIRED per R10, and NOT convertible to a polled-state query: the game consumes AT MOST ONE hotkey per frame, and a 'what is held right now' interface would change that semantics silently. WHAT A HOST SUPPLIES: a FIFO of key events, drained one per call, in the order the player produced them.

llm_input_key_queue_empty.reason: Report whether the key queue has anything in it, without consuming. The tactical frame asks this before dequeuing; a host that answers wrongly either drops the player's input or feeds a stale/garbage event into an order. It measures as tact-only in the translated tree, which is a translation-frontier artefact -- the original has SIX non-tact callers (llm_strat_input_update, llm_ui_menu_transition_settle, llm_ui_modal_key_pump, ...).

llm_input_mouse_buttons_get.reason: The current mouse button mask. Pushed-model exception by necessity: buttons are level state, not events, and the game samples them per frame. WHAT A HOST SUPPLIES: the mask as of the frame libmh is stepping, stable for the duration of that frame -- a mask that changes mid-frame produces selections that begin and end in different worlds.

llm_input_mouse_delta_pump.reason: Accumulated mouse movement since the last call, and it is a PUMP: the act of asking clears the accumulator. A host that returns absolute position here makes the cursor accelerate away.

llm_lobby_map_recv_step_stub.reason: DELETED FROM THE SURFACE at SIMABI-HOOKS (2026-09-10). Empty at 0x0049bfa5 (stack probe + return, re-verified in the DB); one site, in llm_strat_session_begin_multi, void and unconditional. The same-name loop in docs/mp-bootstrap.md is untranslated lobby code, not this path. Nothing may call it again.

The entry was three statements -- GAME_MODE_SAVED = GAME_MODE @0x004c85c8, llm_net_lockstep_wait_player_overlay_show @0x004c85e8, GAME_MODE = 8 @0x004c85ed -- i.e. the same shape as the four LIB-ABI stage E split, which missed it only because it hangs off sim_order_dispatch's calls struct. Ordering law at the site: read, clear, then emit, and NO emit on the answered arm (an answer exists only while the LOCKSTEP_SYNC list is installed, so the original's arm guard cannot hold there) -- that arm reproduces the original's tail overlay_dismiss at its own instant instead. Hosted sink routes the record onto the thunk synchronously at emit (R5-exact); its poll half then reads the -1 libmh just wrote and does nothing.

llm_net_transport_recv.reason: Receive one queued inbound lockstep packet, if any: the inbound half of transport_send. WHAT A HOST SUPPLIES: a NON-BLOCKING poll that hands libmh the next packet from any peer with the sender's identity, and reports 'nothing yet' without waiting -- libmh calls it from the turn engine every step and a blocking implementation stalls the sim. Per-peer ordering must be preserved; the lockstep protocol assumes it.

llm_net_transport_send.reason: REQUIRED, `net` group. THE ONE OF THE SEVEN `dead`-class stubs THAT IS A LIVE SEAM, and the class was wrong for it rather than merely imprecise: retail's body @0x0049ba8d is gutted, but mh.dll REPLACES it (MH_EXPORT_REPLACE_llm_net_transport_send; seams/net_seams.cpp binds ADDR_GAME_SEND to MH_Seam_GameSend), so the call libmh makes in the hosted configuration reaches the restored TCP transport, not a stub. `dead` said the opposite. What a host must supply: send `len` bytes of `buf` to every other peer in the session, reliably and in order -- it is the outbound half of transport_recv, which is already a required entry beside it. A host that no-ops it has a lockstep that never advances. Reclassed at LIFT-TABLE S6 (2026-09-09); its three sites in lockstep/tx_emit{,_chat,_ctrl}.cpp were the last raw VA calls in the emitters.

The sites: sim/resid/sim_scenario_planet_clone.cpp widens the (possibly truncated) map name into _G_LLM_STRAT_SCENARIO_PLANET_NAME_W (MF_VIEW, 32 B) and publishes the RETURNED pointer into G_TEXT_PTRS[0xa8]; save/save_live.cpp's pre-v5 legacy-save upgrade widens 30 ANSI records into MESSAGE_QUEUE (MF_VIEW|MF_SAVE, 7200 B), a read-side path unreachable from any file this build wrote. NOT ALLOCATING -- the correction this row carries: dst is caller-supplied at both sites, so the old 'allocating ... the allocation must outlive the call' wording described how long the CALLER's buffer must stay valid, not a heap contract, and a host that allocated here would leak on every call.

map_ReadMap_pre.reason: PRE-FORK ONLY (DEFER-BLOB). Load a planet's map for the session about to begin. A parse, not a byte service -- see cfg_ReadMapFile -- and it has a runtime writer into the hashed Planets record (tlo_file at +0x20e), so it is not read-only from the sim's point of view either. Both libmh sites pass a planet index and read NOTHING back (sim/resid/sim_planet_session_begin.cpp:97, sim/resid/sim_session_begin_multi.cpp:139): every output lands in globals. WHAT LIB-WORLD'S BLOB MUST CARRY TO RETIRE THIS ENTRY, re-verified at SIMABI-MAPIO 2026-09-10 down the callee chain @0x004552d6 -- AND THE EARLIER FIELD LIST WAS AN UNDERCOUNT: this entry does not merely resolve a tileset name, it INSTALLS THE WHOLE PLANET, in three steps. (1) map_FillDefaults @0x0045603e bulk-zeroes ~25 per-planet regions -- units, buildings, tile_objects, soldiers, projectile pool, order queue, resources, passable, fog_of_war, productions/mines/turrets/labs/unit_storage, path buffers -- and carries the storage_stats/death_anim_table PRESERVE-BUG recorded on its plate, so the blob must reproduce the state that bug actually leaves, not a plausible one. (2) map_ReadMap @0x004a3251 sets the `width`/`height` globals and calls llm_map_setup_dimensions (masks DERIVED, not carried -- see cfg_ReadMapFile), then strcpy's the .MP header's tileset name into Planets[index].tlo_file (+0x20e, HIDX_PLANETS, HASHED). (3) THE SIX PLANES, which are the actual payload: main terrain -> tile_objects (RID_TILE_OBJECTS = HIDX_TILE_OBJECTS 21, hashed, both halves of the 8-byte record); passable -> passable (RID_PASSABLE) -- CORRECTED 2026-09-11 (LIB-WORLD, measured): the llm_map_build_regions nav decomposition it also installs is a HEAP-POINTER GRAPH (MAP_REGION_GRID alone 178,851 differing bytes across two otherwise lockstep-hash-identical captures, plus MAP_REGION_BY_INDEX and the pool heads) and physically CANNOT be carried by a bound-region blob -- the importing host must REBUILD it from the carried passable plane, exactly like the torus masks; it is the same decomposition map_load_regions decodes on the save path; the half-res plane -> _G_LLM_MAP_HALFRES_GRID (RID_MAP_HALFRES_GRID); the f2 object list -> _G_LLM_MAP_OBJECTS (RID_MAP_OBJECTS) with chain heads stamped back into tile_objects; the resource-yield plane -> resources (RID_RESOURCES), scaled by Planets[idx].source_mul; the landing spots -> _G_LLM_STRAT_LANDING_SPOTS (RID_STRAT_LANDING_SPOTS). Every one of those is a BOUND REGION, which is precisely why D-E5's fixture shape (dump every bound region at step 0) can retire this entry when it cannot retire the save-container entries. TWO TAILS DO NOT RETIRE WITH IT: planet_tlo_load (llm_planet_tlo_load), called here, is its own entry and survives on its save-path caller (save/save_live.cpp:463, the one R3-consumed return in the group); llm_gfx_load_planet_extra_sprite_banks, also called here, already left the table at SIMABI-NOTIFY as INV_PLANET_EXTRA_SPRITE_BANKS -- the ORIGINAL still calls the original, which is a fact about the pre-fork binary, not a double-fire in libmh. THE NAME IS DELIBERATELY THE ORIGINAL ONE (SIMABI-NAMES, 2026-09-10), and it is the pre-fork stamp: every other surviving entry was renamed to an abstract name that promises a permanent host contract, which is exactly the promise a DEFER-BLOB row does not make -- this entry is scheduled to LEAVE the surface when LIB-WORLD's blob carries the outputs listed above. An abstract name here would read as an obligation a standalone host must implement forever; the original callee's name says instead 'this is the pre-fork binary's own parse, still here because the blob is not'.

utils_abort.reason: Terminate the process. IT MUST NOT RETURN: libmh calls it on unrecoverable asset and state errors and the code after the call assumes it is unreachable. Nine translation units reach it. (The routing census reports 0 direct callers, which is a blind spot rather than a fact -- utils_abort is not a node in the trimmed call graph at all; its site_modules field, a source scan, has it right.) A host that wants to survive the condition must unwind on its own side; returning here resumes a body that has already decided it cannot continue. THE NAME (SIMABI-NAMES, 2026-09-10): the sim table calls this entry `fatal`; the original callee is `utils_abort`, and the FROZEN tact table keeps that spelling for its own copy. So the two tables no longer share a member name -- the printed overlap goes 1 -> 0 -- while both still bind the same original body in the hosted configuration. That is duplication working as designed (the same shape as GetResourseFilePtr/asset_read at SIMABI-VFS), not a lost share.

utils_close_file.reason: Close a handle from vfs_open, flushing any buffered writes. libmh does not read a result, so this returns nothing -- the original's was already discarded at every site.

utils_open_file.reason: Open `path` and return a handle libmh passes back to vfs_read/write/seek/tell/close; 0 means failure. `mode` is 0 = read-binary or 1 = write-binary-truncate -- the only two the game asks for, so it is an enum rather than a mode string (mh.dll's binder synthesises retail's "rb"/"wb"). Paths cross VERBATIM -- the 2026-09-03 decision kept direct file paths for this pass rather than abstracting to a virtual filesystem -- so a host may map or sandbox them, but it must accept the game's own spelling.

utils_read_from_file.reason: Read up to `n` bytes at the handle's current position into `dst` and advance it; return the byte count, or a negative value on error. A short read must be REPORTED, not padded: the save reader treats the byte count as the truth about what the file contained.

utils_wide_to_short_str.reason: Convert a wide (UTF-16) string to the local ANSI code page into the CALLER's buffer, and return that buffer. STRICT CONTRACT (SIMABI-STRING 2026-09-10): it is utils_w_strlen + utils_WideStringToAscii @0x004cf2dc, i.e. WideCharToMultiByte(CP_ACP, 0, src, n, dst, n, <default char @0x00661524>, ...) -- reproduce THOSE bytes, not something equivalent. ITS RESULT FEEDS HASHED SIM STATE: its libmh site (sim/resid/sim_start_tutorial.cpp) writes player_desc[1].name, inside the 416-byte `players` slice HIDX_PLAYERS. A host that no-ops it leaves that name unwritten and diverges on the very next state hash, and one that substitutes a plausible truncation diverges the moment the text table is not ASCII. THE 'ONE ENTRY IN THIS TABLE' CLAIM THIS ROW USED TO MAKE IS CORRECTED (2026-09-10): wide_to_local_bytes feeds a hashed region too (HIDX_STRAT_PLAYERS, via llm_strat_player_profile_init's name copy) -- there are two strict codecs, not one. This row recorded the entry twice as an internalize case on the strength of its name; both readings were wrong about the mechanism, which is why the trap is spelled out rather than summarised. MEASURED, not argued: simtest's sim_start_tutorial T10 flips one byte of this entry's returned buffer at that sim site and the `players` slice hash moves, and reverting it restores the hash exactly. THE CP_ACP MULTIPLAYER HAZARD IS A NAMED DEFERRED DECISION OWNED BY LIB-FORK, on the llm_strat_rng_seed_wallclock_seconds precedent -- see wide_to_local_bytes's row for the full statement; never vendor a fixed codec silently. RULED 2026-09-12 (F0-CPACP, user): KEEP CP_ACP -- retail-faithful, the same-locale MP requirement documented; the post-fork direction is full UTF-8/multilanguage text (docs/fork-plan.md, post-F5), which retires this question rather than re-answering it.

utils_write_to_file.reason: Write `n` bytes at the handle's current position and advance it; return the byte count written, or a NEGATIVE value if the write did not fully happen -- a partial write is a failure, not a number the save writer knows how to use. Save byte-identity is a permanent guarantee of the frozen side, so this must not transform anything on the way through.
